path_decisions.rationale: RSI adaptive uses mean RSI at all entry points (not per-trade), and profit_target_exit only handles long — backtest edge cases reveal the short-position gap directly
BacktestEngine is long-only; profit_target_exit never exits shorts — profit target calibration is the node that directly exposes the direction-aware exit gap
Profit targets feed into consolidated signals; discovered that strategy_hit_rates is never populated at runtime in TradingSession — signal weighting is effectively disabled
Signal weights feed into position sizing; discovered strategy_win_rates and strategy_risk_budgets are also never wired in TradingSession — per-strategy features are dead code

evidence: quantflow/strategy/templates/_runtime.py:167 — profit_target_exit checks close >= entry_price * (1+pct), never handles short (close <= entry_price * (1-pct))
quantflow/strategy/research/backtest.py:62 — comment: 'Simulates a simple long-only portfolio' — BacktestEngine cannot backtest short trades
quantflow/strategy/templates/trend_following.py:260-266 — RSI adaptive uses rsi[entries].mean() across all entry bars, not per-entry RSI — one global multiplier instead of per-trade adaptation

quantflow/strategy/engine.py:54-55 — RiskEngine(config.risk) and PositionSizer(method='kelly', max_position_pct=config.risk.position_limit_pct * 100) — strategy_risk_budgets, strategy_win_rates never passed
quantflow/signal/risk_engine.py:104-108 — _check_strategy_budget sums ALL positions into strategy_exposure regardless of which strategy opened them; Position model has no strategy_id field
quantflow/strategy/engine.py:58 — max_position_pct=config.risk.position_limit_pct * 100 — 0.20 * 100 = 20.0 means 2000% cap, effectively no position limit
quantflow/signal/generator.py:57-68 — consolidate_signals accepts strategy_hit_rates param but TradingSession never calls it with hit rate data
quantflow/signal/position_sizer.py:41-53 — size() accepts strategy_win_rates param but TradingSession._process_signal (engine.py:208) calls size(signal, portfolio) without win rates
quantflow/config/default.yaml:36 — position_limit_pct: 0.20 (20%) but engine.py multiplies by 100 creating 2000% effective cap
quantflow/strategy/templates/mean_reversion.py:138 — entries combines long+short entries but profit_target_exit only handles long profit targets

candidate_solution.summary: 6 critical bottlenecks: (1) profit_target_exit short-direction bug, (2) RSI adaptive uses mean not per-trade, (3) BacktestEngine long-only, (4) strategy_hit_rates/win_rates/risk_budgets never wired in TradingSession, (5) risk budget sums all positions not per-strategy, (6) max_position_pct *100 bug creates 2000% cap

bottlenecks.title: profit_target_exit only handles long positions — short trades never hit profit target
bottlenecks.description: profit_target_exit() in _runtime.py:167 checks `close >= entry_price * (1.0 + profit_take_pct)` which only works for longs. For short entries (mean_reversion, funding_rate generate Direction.SHORT), the profit target condition should be `close <= entry_price * (1.0 - profit_take_pct)`. This means all short-position profit targets are silently never triggered, forcing exits via max_holding_bars timeout at a loss or break-even. Estimated impact: mean_reversion short-side win rate reduced by ~15-25% since profitable short trades hold until timeout instead of capturing profit early.
bottlenecks.fix: Add direction parameter to profit_target_exit: for short positions, check close <= entry_price * (1 - profit_take_pct). Pass direction from entries context.

bottlenecks.title: RSI adaptive profit target uses mean RSI across all entries, not per-entry RSI
bottlenecks.description: In trend_following.py:260-266, RSI adaptive computes `rsi[entries].mean()` — a single average across all entry bars. This creates one global multiplier (0.8x or 1.2x) for all trades in the backtest, rather than adapting per-trade. A trade entered at RSI=80 gets the same profit target as one entered at RSI=55 if the average is below 70. This defeats the purpose of RSI-adaptive targets and can even make targets worse (e.g., if most entries are RSI 50-65, the adaptive check never triggers).
bottlenecks.fix: Compute effective_pct per entry: when an entry signal fires, look up the RSI at that specific entry bar and apply 0.8x/1.2x scaling individually. This requires a vectorized approach: for each entry, track the RSI at entry and apply the scaling from that point forward.

bottlenecks.title: BacktestEngine is long-only — cannot evaluate short-side strategies correctly
bottlenecks.description: backtest.py:62 states 'Simulates a simple long-only portfolio'. Entry → buy, exit → sell. For short entries (mean_reversion, funding_rate), the backtest enters long regardless. This means all backtest win rate numbers for strategies that generate SHORT signals are inflated/incorrect — they're actually running the opposite direction. This is a fundamental measurement error that makes the current win rate unreliable.
bottlenecks.fix: Extend BacktestEngine to support direction-aware positions: short entries sell first and buy to close. Track position direction separately. Or at minimum, split entries into long_entries and short_entries and process each with correct P&L calculation.

bottlenecks.title: strategy_hit_rates and strategy_win_rates never populated in TradingSession — signal consolidation and Kelly sizing use defaults
bottlenecks.description: SignalGenerator.consolidate_signals() accepts strategy_hit_rates (generator.py:57) and PositionSizer.size() accepts strategy_win_rates (position_sizer.py:41), but TradingSession._process_signal() at engine.py:208 calls `self._position_sizer.size(signal, portfolio)` without passing strategy_win_rates, and never calls consolidate_signals with strategy_hit_rates. The 'strength-weighted consolidation' and 'per-strategy Kelly sizing' features from the win-rate improvement are effectively dead code at runtime. All strategies default to hit_rate=0.5 for consolidation and win_rate=0.5 for Kelly, making these features no-ops.
bottlenecks.fix: 1) Add a strategy_stats dict to TradingSession that accumulates per-strategy win/loss counts. 2) Pass strategy_stats to consolidate_signals and size() calls. 3) Compute rolling win_rate per strategy from closed trade outcomes.

bottlenecks.title: RiskEngine._check_strategy_budget sums ALL positions, not per-strategy positions
bottlenecks.description: risk_engine.py:104-108 iterates portfolio.positions.values() and sums every position's value into strategy_exposure, regardless of which strategy opened the position. The Position model (common/models.py:80) has no strategy_id field, so there's no way to attribute positions to strategies. This means if you set trend_following budget=15%, ANY strategy's positions count against trend_following's 15% limit. With 5 positions each at 5%, total exposure = 25%, which exceeds the 15% budget — blocking trend_following from opening new trades even though its own exposure is only 5%.
bottlenecks.fix: 1) Add strategy_id field to Position model. 2) When opening positions, tag with originating strategy_id. 3) In _check_strategy_budget, filter positions by strategy_id matching signal.strategy_id before summing exposure.

bottlenecks.title: max_position_pct * 100 bug creates 2000% effective cap — position limit is disabled
bottlenecks.description: engine.py:58 sets `max_position_pct=config.risk.position_limit_pct * 100`. Since config.risk.position_limit_pct = 0.20 (from default.yaml:36), this results in max_position_pct = 20.0. PositionSizer line 72 computes `max_notional = total_value * 20.0` = 20x portfolio value as the cap, which is never hit. The intended 20% position limit is completely bypassed. This allows oversized positions that increase volatility and reduce win rate through excessive concentration risk.
bottlenecks.fix: Remove the * 100 multiplication. The value 0.20 is already a fraction. Change engine.py:58 to `max_position_pct=config.risk.position_limit_pct`.

calibration_gaps.issue: Code default and YAML are out of sync; YAML says 15% but code defaults to 10%. Also, the RSI-adaptive multiplier (0.8x/1.2x) has only 2 breakpoints at RSI 30/70 — a continuous function would better capture the gradient.

YAML config specifies 1.5 but code defaults to 3.0/2.5. A multiplier of 3.0 ATR is very wide — typical trend systems use 2.0-2.5 ATR trailing stops. 3.0 ATR may let winning trades reverse significantly before stopping out.

With only 3 conditions (vol_ok, RSI, BB), min_conditions=2 means ANY 2 of 3 triggers entry. This allows entries without volume confirmation (RSI+BB only), which are lower quality. Consider requiring vol_ok as a mandatory filter rather than optional.

interaction_effects.issue: In trend_following.py:288-292, when profit_exits fires, in_pos resets to False and highest resets to close. But trailing_exits is computed AFTER the loop, so the trailing stop may also fire on the same bar as profit_target, creating a double-exit signal. While this is OR'd (line 294), the real issue is that the trailing stop track uses close prices, not the actual entry/high tracking for a trailing stop — it should track the highest high since entry, not highest close.

trend_following.py:164-167 counts conditions including RSI<70. When RSI>70, rsi_ok_long is False, reducing the condition count. But the RSI adaptive (line 263) then tightens the profit target because avg_entry_rsi>70. This creates a contradiction: the system avoids entries when RSI>70 (reducing count below min_conditions), but when entries DO happen with RSI>70 (rare edge case), it tightens targets — the adaptive logic almost never activates because RSI>70 entries are blocked by min_conditions.

missing_mechanisms.description: No market regime detection (trending vs ranging). Trend_following performs poorly in ranging markets but there's no mechanism to reduce position size or skip entries when regime is unfavorable. Top quant systems use ADX or Hurst exponent for regime filtering.

All exits are binary (full close). No partial exit at first target (e.g., exit 50% at 1R, trail the rest). This leaves unrealized profit on the table and reduces win rate because winning trades that reverse before the full target are counted as full losses rather than partial wins.

priority_ranking.reason: All per-strategy features (hit rates, Kelly sizing, risk budgets) are dead code — fixing this unlocks 3 features at once
Short-side profit targets never fire — direct win rate killer for mean_reversion and funding_rate
BacktestEngine long-only means all win rate measurements are unreliable for short strategies
Risk budget blocks all trades once total exposure exceeds any single strategy budget
Position limit completely disabled by *100 bug — allows oversized positions
RSI adaptive per-entry would improve but current mean-based approach still provides some benefit

notes: YAML config parameters (trailing_stop_atr_multiplier, take_profit_pct, stop_loss_pct) are defined in YAML but NOT read by strategy __init__ methods — strategies only read from the params dict passed at construction, so YAML exit section values are silently ignored. This means even if YAML is calibrated, strategies use code defaults unless explicitly overridden through the params dict.
